report.incidentSummary: At market open on 2026-10-19 09:15 IST (03:45 UTC), stock order placement suffered elevated error rates (~22.5%) and high latency (p95 > 2,000ms). The on-call SRE suspected an external broker outage based on a similar incident last month. However, broker-connector and broker-api were fully healthy. The actual cause was client-side database connection pool exhaustion in order-service resulting from configuration change CHG-48221 deployed on Friday 2026-10-16, which reduced db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20. When market-open order traffic spiked to ~29,210 orders/min, the 20 connections were instantly saturated, causing orders to time out after 1,000ms waiting for a connection and fail with HTTP 503. The incident self-resolved around 04:26 UTC (09:56 IST) as opening order volume subsided below 8,000 orders/min.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service's database connection pool ceiling (db.pool.max_connections) from 100 to 20 on Friday 2026-10-16. During the subsequent market open on Monday 2026-10-19 at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), order traffic surged to 29,210 orders/min (~487 orders/sec). This arrival rate saturated the 20-connection pool, driving connection acquisition wait times above the 1,000ms acquisition timeout and causing ~22.5% of stock orders to fail with HTTP 503 ('timeout acquiring DB connection (pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms)'). The broker-connector and external broker API were completely healthy.

hypotheses.cause: order-service database connection pool exhaustion caused by CHG-48221 reducing db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20, which proved insufficient to handle the ~29,210 orders/min (~487 orders/sec) market-open surge, causing connection acquisition timeouts (1000ms) and ~22.5% order placement 503 failures.
hypotheses.rationale: The configuration change CHG-48221 reduced the connection pool from 100 to 20 on Friday evening. Monday's market open was the first trading session since the change. Saturated pool metrics (pegged at 20/20), wait times exceeding the 1000ms connection timeout, and direct log messages citing 'timeout acquiring DB connection (pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms)' directly explain all symptoms and recovery.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream broker API degradation or rate limiting causing order failures and latency at market open (reporter's initial suspicion based on past incident PIR-2008).
hypotheses.rationale: Although PIR-2008 presented similar symptoms of ~25% order failure rate at market open due to a broker exchange gateway outage, broker-connector metrics in this incident demonstrated a flat 0.20% error rate, normal upstream latencies (140-200ms), and 0 rate limits.

hypotheses.cause: Primary database instance capacity saturation or table lock contention under high market-open load.
hypotheses.rationale: Database CPU was moderate (~37%), active connections were stable (~138), lock wait times were negligible (~4ms), and slow queries were low (0-7/min). The bottleneck was client-side connection pool limits in order-service, not the database.

facts.statement: On Friday 2026-10-16 at 13:35:00 UTC (19:05 IST, post-market), configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 to reduce idle connections on the primary database.
At market open on Monday 2026-10-19 at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), order volume to order-service surged from ~5,024 orders/min (~131 req/s) at 03:44 UTC to 29,210 orders/min (~710 req/s) at 03:45 UTC.
order-service db_pool_in_use rose from ~13.85 connections pre-open to 20.01 at 03:45 UTC and remained pegged at exactly the 20-connection pool ceiling until 04:25 UTC.
order-service db_pool_wait_ms rose from ~2.57 ms pre-open to 1,045 ms at 03:46 UTC and stayed above 950 ms (peaking at 1,151 ms) throughout the incident window.
order-service logged repeated ERROR messages with status 503 stating: 'timeout acquiring DB connection (pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms)'.
Between 03:46 UTC and 04:23 UTC, order-service error_rate jumped from 0.58% to ~22.5%, latency_p95_ms escalated from ~300 ms to over 2,000 ms, and order_success_rate fell from 99.2% to ~72%.

During the incident window, broker-connector error_rate remained steady at ~0.20%, latency_p95_ms remained between 140-250 ms, upstream_latency_p95_ms remained between 140-200 ms, and rate_limited_count was 0.
During the incident window, the primary database remained healthy with cpu_utilization at ~37%, db_lock_wait_ms at ~4 ms, active_connections steady at ~138, and slow_queries_per_min low at 0-7/min.

At 04:26 UTC, as order volume naturally tapered to 7,998 orders/min, db_pool_in_use dropped to 17.87, db_pool_wait_ms dropped to 3.00 ms, order-service error_rate normalized to 0.43%, and order_success_rate recovered to 99.27%.

inferences.statement: The on-call SRE's suspicion of a broker outage was an anchoring bias caused by past incident PIR-2008 (2026-09-21), which exhibited an identical ~25% failure rate at market open but was caused by an exchange gateway outage.
CHG-48221 was deployed after market close on Friday (13:35 UTC / 19:05 IST), meaning its impact on peak trading load was not exercised until Monday's market open at 09:15 IST.

At ~29,000 orders/min (~483 orders/sec), even modest per-order database query holding times (~45-50ms) require over 22-25 concurrent connections according to Little's Law, making a maximum pool of 20 mathematically insufficient to avoid queuing and timeouts.

timeline.event: Configuration change CHG-48221 executed by r.iyer reducing order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 after market close on Friday.
Pre-market open baseline: order-service handling ~5,024 orders/min with 0.36% error rate, 13.85 connections in use, and 2.57ms DB pool wait time.
Market opens (09:15 IST). Order traffic spikes to 29,210 orders/min (~710 req/s); order-service db_pool_in_use hits the 20/20 pool ceiling.
Connection acquisition wait time jumps to 1,045ms; order-service error rate surges to 22.76% with HTTP 503 errors logging DB connection acquisition timeouts; latency p95 climbs to 2,428ms.
Incident reported by On-call SRE suspecting external broker outage based on past incident PIR-2008.
Peak opening traffic begins to abate; orders decline to 9,480 orders/min and error rate falls to 15.12%.
Order volume drops to 7,998 orders/min; db_pool_in_use drops below maximum to 17.87; db_pool_wait_ms normalizes to 3.00ms; error rate falls to 0.43% and order success rate recovers to 99.27%.

confidence.rationale: The root cause is definitively established by configuration change CHG-48221, direct error logs indicating connection pool acquisition timeouts at 20/20 in use, exact metric alignment of db_pool_in_use pegging at 20 connections and db_pool_wait_ms exceeding the 1000ms acquisition timeout during the 29k orders/min market open surge, and comprehensive negative evidence ruling out broker degradation and database saturation.

gaps.description: The query for order-service cpu_utilization returned a partial response with some unread records.
gaps.impact: Negligible, as the 105 returned 1-minute buckets showed peak CPU of 71.59% at 03:45 UTC, confirming order-service was not CPU-saturated.

recommendedActions.action: Revert or scale up order-service db.pool.max_connections from 20 back to 100 (or at least 50-100 based on peak order arrival calculations).
recommendedActions.rationale: The reduced pool size of 20 will cause identical connection pool exhaustion during tomorrow's 09:15 IST market open surge.
recommendedActions.verification: Inspect order-service configuration to verify db.pool.max_connections >= 100; monitor db_pool_in_use and db_pool_wait_ms at tomorrow's market open to ensure wait times remain < 10ms.

recommendedActions.action: Implement an alert for order-service database connection pool utilization (e.g. db_pool_in_use >= 18 for > 1 minute, or db_pool_wait_ms > 100ms).
recommendedActions.rationale: Neither connection pool saturation nor acquisition wait times alerted on-call before order failures reached SEV1 severity.
recommendedActions.verification: Review Prometheus/alertmanager configuration for the new rule and trigger a synthetic alert test in staging.

recommendedActions.action: Enforce load testing validation and change review guidelines for connection pool adjustments on Tier-1 transactional services.
recommendedActions.rationale: CHG-48221 was implemented to reduce idle connections without evaluating or load-testing the impact on market-open peak throughput.
recommendedActions.verification: Ensure engineering RFC/runbook requires capacity calculations against peak historical QPS prior to merging pool downsizing changes.

recommendedActions.action: Update the market-open order failure on-call triage runbook to check order-service db_pool_wait_ms and db_pool_in_use before escalating to broker partners.
recommendedActions.rationale: Triage initially anchored on an external broker outage due to past incident PIR-2008, delaying identification of internal pool exhaustion.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify runbook documentation includes links to order-service connection pool dashboards and checks.

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** completed · **Confidence:** 0.98 · **Written by:** baseline agent

## Summary

The broker-connector and external broker API were completely healthy.

## Facts
- On Friday 2026-10-16 at 13:35:00 UTC (19:05 IST, post-market), configuration change CHG-48221 reduced order-service db.pool.max_connections from 100 to 20 to reduce idle connections on the primary database. [ev_22]
- At market open on Monday 2026-10-19 at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), order volume to order-service surged from ~5,024 orders/min (~131 req/s) at 03:44 UTC to 29,210 orders/min (~710 req/s) at 03:45 UTC. [ev_14, ev_19]
- order-service db_pool_in_use rose from ~13.85 connections pre-open to 20.01 at 03:45 UTC and remained pegged at exactly the 20-connection pool ceiling until 04:25 UTC. [ev_12]
- order-service db_pool_wait_ms rose from ~2.57 ms pre-open to 1,045 ms at 03:46 UTC and stayed above 950 ms (peaking at 1,151 ms) throughout the incident window. [ev_5]
- order-service logged repeated ERROR messages with status 503 stating: 'timeout acquiring DB connection (pool 20/20 in use, waited 1000ms)'. [ev_6]
- Between 03:46 UTC and 04:23 UTC, order-service error_rate jumped from 0.58% to ~22.5%, latency_p95_ms escalated from ~300 ms to over 2,000 ms, and order_success_rate fell from 99.2% to ~72%. [ev_3, ev_13, ev_24]
- During the incident window, broker-connector error_rate remained steady at ~0.20%, latency_p95_ms remained between 140-250 ms, upstream_latency_p95_ms remained between 140-200 ms, and rate_limited_count was 0. [ev_4, ev_11, ev_15, ev_16]
- During the incident window, the primary database remained healthy with cpu_utilization at ~37%, db_lock_wait_ms at ~4 ms, active_connections steady at ~138, and slow_queries_per_min low at 0-7/min. [ev_7, ev_8, ev_9, ev_10]
- At 04:26 UTC, as order volume naturally tapered to 7,998 orders/min, db_pool_in_use dropped to 17.87, db_pool_wait_ms dropped to 3.00 ms, order-service error_rate normalized to 0.43%, and order_success_rate recovered to 99.27%. [ev_3, ev_5, ev_12, ev_14, ev_24]

## Inferences
- The on-call SRE's suspicion of a broker outage was an anchoring bias caused by past incident PIR-2008 (2026-09-21), which exhibited an identical ~25% failure rate at market open but was caused by an exchange gateway outage. [ev_2]
- CHG-48221 was deployed after market close on Friday (13:35 UTC / 19:05 IST), meaning its impact on peak trading load was not exercised until Monday's market open at 09:15 IST. [ev_12, ev_14, ev_22]
- At ~29,000 orders/min (~483 orders/sec), even modest per-order database query holding times (~45-50ms) require over 22-25 concurrent connections according to Little's Law, making a maximum pool of 20 mathematically insufficient to avoid queuing and timeouts. [ev_5, ev_12, ev_14]
